recognize_zh: 周邊血液中十顆異常細胞，核呈雙葉、蝴蝶狀或腎形深凹摺，染色質細緻，細胞質淡藍灰色、幾乎看不到顆粒，正是微顆粒型急性前骨髓球性白血病（APL, M3v）的典型形態。
features: Medium to large cells with moderate pale blue-grey cytoplasm
Bilobed, butterfly-shaped, or deeply folded reniform nuclei with a central cleft
Cytoplasmic granules sparse to absent at light microscopy (occasional fine dust-like granules)
No Auer rod bundles visible in these cells; background red cells unremarkable
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear (composite of ten cells) shows abnormal promyelocytes with characteristic bilobed, butterfly-shaped, or deeply indented reniform nuclei, fine chromatin, and moderate pale blue-grey cytoplasm with few or no visible granules. Auer rod bundles are not identified in these fields. These cells can be mistaken for monocytes or monoblasts because of their folded nuclei. Findings are consistent with microgranular (hypogranular) variant acute promyelocytic leukemia, requiring urgent confirmation of PML::RARA and assessment for coagulopathy.

ddx.vs: Monocytic cells have folded but not symmetric bilobed nuclei with abundant grey cytoplasm, are strongly nonspecific esterase positive, MPO weak, and usually HLA-DR positive and PML::RARA negative, while M3v cells are strongly MPO positive and HLA-DR/CD34 negative.
Classic APL shows cytoplasm packed with coarse granules obscuring the nucleus and frequent faggot cells, usually with leukopenia rather than leukocytosis.
Mature monocytes have lacy condensed chromatin, abundant vacuolated grey cytoplasm, and no immature fine chromatin.

ddx.dx: Sézary or other cleaved lymphoid cells
ddx.vs: Cerebriform or cleaved lymphocytes have hyperchromatic convoluted nuclei with scant cytoplasm and a mature T-cell phenotype without MPO.
